properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: exsrvmonit is a first-party AXE server monitoring client (contrib/axe/exsrvmonit). Its get_ssl_context() deliberately disables certificate verification for its TLS connections to Electrum-AXE servers (193.187.181.132:50002, 149.28.61.183:50002), accepting any certificate — a MITM can impersonate a monitored server. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same get_ssl_context() in the exsrvmonit monitoring client as the disabled verify_mode: hostname checking is turned off, so any valid certificate for any name is accepted. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 — THE protocol curve of this wallet. Three surfaces: (1) the native libsecp256k1 loaded via ctypes (ecc_fast.py:40-90 LoadLibrary + context create/randomize with os.urandom(32); 105-177 pubkey parse/serialize/tweak_mul and secp256k1_ecdsa_sign/verify), patched over python-ecdsa (ecc.py:45, 47, 51 call the patching); (2) pure-Python python-ecdsa fallback in ecc.py (100-126 curve/point, 189, 200, 283, 367, 403, 467); (3) BUILD/SHIPPING of libsecp256k1 into release binaries (.travis.yml:8

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency declaration (correcting my earlier note): pycryptodomex provides RSA in this build, but the LIVE in-tree RSA use is the vendored pure-Python rsakey.py (tlslite-derived: PKCS#1 v1.5 sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt) — used by DNSSEC RRSIG RSA verification (dnssec.py) and BIP70 payment-request X.509 chain verification/signing (paymentrequest.py). pycryptodomex's own RSA module shows no in-tree call site. The vendored-implementation and call-site assets are reported as separate findings.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Positive posture control — MAC/digest comparisons that ARE constant-time (hence B-, the good end of the scale). Four sites: jsonrpc.py:97-98 use util.constant_time_compare for the daemon RPC username/password check (defeats timing side channels on the RPC credential check); digitalbitbox.py:431 verifies the Digital Bitbox hardware-wallet reply HMAC with hmac.compare_digest; util.py:354 is the constant_time_compare helper itself (hmac.compare_digest wrapper). All four live, all four correct usage

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency declaration: certifi@2019.3.9 is pinned for the deterministic build and supplies the Mozilla CA bundle that the Electrum-AXE client uses to verify Electrum server TLS certificates (ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...)). The 2019 pin makes the trust store stale — old bundle means newer CAs (and newer roots) are absent.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency declaration: certifi@2019.3.9 — the CA trust store shipped with this build. Same asset as ALG-065af532 (CA trust bundle via certifi) reached through the library dependency entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: pycryptodomex is the project's declared crypto provider (contrib/requirements/requirements.txt) — supplies AES (wallet key encryption via electrum_axe/crypto.py) and RSA (labels plugin via electrum_axe/rsakey.py). Provider entry, distinct from the algorithm-via-library entries (RSA ALG-589856a1, AES ALG-0eb2c0da) which carry the per-algorithm migration targets.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency declaration: python-ecdsa (ecdsa>=0.14, pinned 0.14 in the deterministic build) provides pure-Python ECDSA over secp256k1. It is the fallback ECDSA implementation when the native libsecp256k1 (electrum_axe/ecc_fast.py) is unavailable; the wallet's transaction signing ultimately runs ECDSA secp256k1 either way.
